title: Fan resolution procedure on globally charted log schemes
statement: Let $R$ be a smooth-functorial saturated fan desingularization [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. There exists a strict etale log blowup procedure $T$ on charted admissible inputs [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. For each such input $X$, there is a fine torsion-free fan $F$ with finite affine cover, and a fan chart $c$ from the terminal log scheme of $T(X)$ to the terminal fan of $R(F)$ [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup]. At each geometric point $t$ of that terminal log scheme, there is a multiplicative isomorphism from the fan stalk at $c(t)$ to the geometric characteristic monoid at $t$, normalized by the Zariski log-section germ equations of IsGeometricComparison.

source.place: Exposé VIII, Remark 3.3.13 and proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp. 108--110.

proof.text: For a globally charted input, use quasi-compactness to restrict the chart fan to a finite union of affine localizations covering its image. Chart stalks are the sharp fs characteristic stalks. Their torsion-free group completions imply torsion-freeness on those affine localization fans. The restriction is therefore a ResolutionInput. For the empty input use the empty fan.

Apply the given R to this input and lift its finite ordered fan tower by log_fan_chart_blowup. Centers are the prescribed inverse-image log ideals and are nonempty coherent. Delete exactly whole-monoid centers: the identity principalizes a whole ideal after every morphism, so uniqueness in the saturated log blowup universal property makes these stages log identities. Transport the final fan chart and its normalized geometric comparisons through the resulting log isomorphism of terminal levels. Retain proper principal centers.

Apply strict_fan_chart_local_comparison to two charts and the identity log map. On its neighbourhoods their target fans are identified through affine localizations. The identity and composition laws of R identify the ordered localized fan centers. Pulling back these centers gives the same log ideals. Universal log blowups give unique comparisons at every level; their uniqueness proves agreement on overlaps and the cocycle law. Glue the centers and level maps inside the already charted input. The tower is independent of the chosen chart.

For a strict etale map of globally charted inputs, use the same chart-local comparison and strict pullback of log fan towers. The identified ideals give Cartesian blowup squares. Delete exactly whole pulled ideals to obtain the order-preserving comparison indices, retained centers and deleted identity steps. Uniqueness of blowup factorizations gives the identity and composition equations. Apply also to component inclusions into finite disjoint unions, using R on the disjoint union fan to synchronize the ordering. This constructs T on the charted domain as a property of X, with the terminal chart and geometric comparisons from the lifted R-tower.

proof_origin.place: Exposé VIII, Remark 3.3.13 and proof of Theorem 3.3.15, printed pp. 108--110. The terminal-stalk descent argument is expanded from the descent reduction.

theorem exists_charted_fan_resolution_procedure
    (R : FineFan.SmoothFunctorialDesingularization.{u}) :
    ∃ T : StrictEtaleLogBlowupProcedure IsChartedLogBlowupInput.{u},
      ∀ (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hX : IsChartedLogBlowupInput X),
        ∃ (F : FineFan.ResolutionInput.{u})
          (c : LogFanChart
            ((T.tower X hX).tower.level (Fin.last (T.tower X hX).tower.length))
            ((R.resolution F).tower.level (Fin.last (R.resolution F).length))),
          ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
            (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶
              ((T.tower X hX).tower.level (Fin.last (T.tower X hX).tower.length)).scheme),
            ∃ e : FineFan.stalk
                ((R.resolution F).tower.level (Fin.last (R.resolution F).length)).space.presheaf
                (c.map.hom.base (t default)) ≃*
                ((T.tower X hX).tower.level
                  (Fin.last (T.tower X hX).tower.length)).logStructure.characteristic t,
              c.IsGeometricComparison t e
